description:
SecurityGroupPolicy defines security groups for pods on EKS Auto Mode
nodes. Matching pods are attached to a branch network interface carrying
exactly the security groups this policy resolves — they do not inherit the
node's security groups.

Matching semantics:
  - If both podSelector and serviceAccountSelector are set, a pod must
    match BOTH (logical AND).
  - If multiple SecurityGroupPolicies in a namespace match the same pod,
    exactly ONE policy applies: the one with the lexically smallest name.
    Policies are never combined for a single pod.

nodeSelector.description:
NodeSelector scopes this policy to nodes by label. When omitted, the
policy applies to every node in the cluster. When set, it currently must
positively reference the "karpenter.sh/nodepool" node label in
matchLabels or matchExpressions (In/Exists only); Exists selects all
NodePools. Broader node-label selection may be permitted in the
future. Only pods scheduled to selected nodes receive branch
interfaces from this policy.

matchExpressions.description: matchExpressions is a list of label selector requirements. The requirements are ANDed.

items.description:
A label selector requirement is a selector that contains values, a key, and an operator that
relates the key and values.

key.description: key is the label key that the selector applies to.

operator.description:
operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values.
Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists and DoesNotExist.

values.description:
values is an array of string values. If the operator is In or NotIn,
the values array must be non-empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist,
the values array must be empty. This array is replaced during a strategic
merge patch.

matchLabels.description:
matchLabels is a map of {key,value} pairs. A single {key,value} in the matchLabels
map is equivalent to an element of matchExpressions, whose key field is "key", the
operator is "In", and the values array contains only "value". The requirements are ANDed.

set, a pod must match both selectors. An empty selector ({}) selects
all pods in the namespace.

securityGroupSelectorTerms.description:
SecurityGroupSelectorTerms is a list of security group selector terms. Terms are ORed.
Each term selects security groups by ID, name, or tags.
The resolved set is hard-rejected above 16 security groups (the EC2
quota ceiling) and surfaced via the SecurityGroupsResolved status
condition. Values within 16 but above your account's security-groups-
per-network-interface quota (default 5) fail at network interface
creation time, surfaced on the pending pod's ResourceClaim events;
affected pods stay pending.

items.description: SecurityGroupSelectorTerm defines a selector for security groups by ID, name, or tags.

id.description: ID is the security group ID (e.g., "sg-0123456789abcdef0").

name.description:
Name is the security group name in EC2.
This value is the name field, which is different from the name tag.

tags.description:
Tags is a map of key/value tags used to select security groups.
Specifying '*' for a value selects all values for a given tag key.

'id' is mutually exclusive, cannot be set with a combination of other fields in securityGroupSelectorTerms
'name' is mutually exclusive, cannot be set with a combination of other fields in securityGroupSelectorTerms

serviceAccountSelector.description:
ServiceAccountSelector selects pods whose ServiceAccount's labels
match. If podSelector is also set, a pod must match both selectors.
An empty selector ({}) matches any ServiceAccount that exists; if the
pod's ServiceAccount cannot be fetched at admission time, the policy
does not match.

lastTransitionTime.description:
lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another.
This should be when the underlying condition changed.  If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable.

message.description:
message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition.
This may be an empty string.

observedGeneration.description:
observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon.
For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date
with respect to the current state of the instance.

reason.description:
reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition.
Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field,
and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API.
The value should be a CamelCase string.
This field may not be empty.

status.description: status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown.

type.description: type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase.

ResolvedSecurityGroupIDs is the list of EC2 security group IDs that the

Updated on SGP create, spec update, or periodic re-resolution (if enabled).
